_readme: THE GAUNTLET — 09-game-modes.md §8. Draft a deck one pick at a time, then ride
it until 12 wins or 3 losses.
WHAT SHIPS. §8 marks this mode Hybrid: Gauntlet Practice offline-now,
competitive Gauntlet online-later. Practice is what this build contains. The
competitive entry cost and its full reward table are still authored here, not
because anything charges or pays them today, but because the rules panel shows
them — a mode that hides what the online version will cost is a mode that can
quietly change its mind later. `entry` is therefore read and displayed and
never debited; `rewards` is displayed in full and paid at `practice.scale`.
WHAT IS NOT HERE, ON PURPOSE.
- The Prism cutoff. §8.1 calls it 'the canonical splash limit', so the draft
reads `economy`-adjacent `deck.prismSplashLimit` out of balance.json rather
than carrying its own copy. Two numbers that must agree are one number.
- The target curve the pick assist steers toward. That is the same curve
`autoBuildDeck` fills, exported from src/engine/deck.ts. A draft that aimed
at a different shape than the game's own deck builder would be teaching a
curve nothing else believes in.
A NOTE ON 'Static'. §8.3's reward table names the crafting material Static;
07-economy-and-monetization.md §2 names it Signal, and Signal is what the shop,
the collection and the save all call it. The column is spelled `signal` here.
The two documents disagree about the word, not the currency.

_note: §8.1. Three leaders from three different factions, then 30 picks of 3.
`spotlightPicks` are 1-based pick numbers, exactly as §8.1 writes them.
`rarity` is rolled ONCE PER PICK and all three cards come from the rolled
rarity. That is what 'offer buckets by pick number' means, and it is what
'curve assist ... never overriding rarity buckets' requires: the bucket is
settled first and the assist only chooses within it.
The two rarity rows must each sum to 1. checkGauntletData asserts it.
`curveAssist` is the weight added to a card whose cost bucket the draft is
short of, per missing copy. At 0 the offer is uniform within its rarity; the
spec says 'softly', and 0.5 means a bucket that is 4 short is 3x as likely to
be offered as one that is full — noticeable over 30 picks, never decisive on
any single one.
§8.2. Play until 12 wins or 3 losses, then the run retires and pays out.
A run can be retired early for the row it has reached.
§8.3. Displayed, never charged — competitive Gauntlet needs a server, and
Practice is free entry by §8.4. `ticket` is the Gauntlet Ticket, the draft
token in 09 §1.3's currency table.
§8.3's table, verbatim. Each row is the WHOLE payout for finishing on that
many wins — the rows are cumulative totals, not increments to be summed.
`cardBackProgress` is §8.3's 'Gauntlet card-back progress +1' on rows 10 and
11. Row 12 does not carry it, and that is the table as written: a 12-win run
is handed the card back outright, so progress toward it is moot.
`cosmetics` are ids into cosmetics.json. §8.3 asks for an ANIMATED Gauntlet
card back at 12 wins; nothing in this build animates a card back, so the
static one is what is paid and the animated upgrade is listed on the screen
as unbuilt with its reason. Paying a still image and calling it animated
would be worse than saying so.
§8.4. The identical draft flow against escalating AI. Free entry, reduced
rewards — '25% of the table, packs excluded, shared with the AI daily cap'.
`scale` multiplies the Clout and Signal columns and nothing else. Packs are
excluded because §8.4 says so. Tickets are excluded because a Gauntlet Ticket
buys one competitive entry and competitive Gauntlet needs a server: paying a
currency with no sink is the inert-reward bug, and banking it would only make
the balance a promise nobody can spend.
The cosmetic rows are NOT scaled. A cosmetic has no 25% of itself, and a
12-win Practice run is the same twelve wins.
The daily cap is NOT here. 09 §3's AI allowance lives in `economy.missions`
and is derived by `aiDailyCap()` from what a win actually pays, because the
cap is a rule about how many matches a day counts, not a Clout constant. The
Gauntlet was the first thing in this build to consume that ceiling; per-match
Clout in every other mode now spends against the same account-wide ledger,
which is what §3 said all along.
`difficultyByWins` is §8.4's 'Casual -> Advanced as wins accumulate', as a
floor table: the highest `minWins` at or below the run's win count wins.
§8.3 hands out 'Gauntlet card-back progress +1' at 10 and 11 wins and never
says how much progress the card back costs. `progressRequired` is therefore
AUTHORED HERE rather than derived from the spec, and this note is the only
honest place to say so: five is four or five deep runs, which puts the back
somewhere past 'won it by accident' and well short of a grind.
The 12-win row grants the back outright and skips the counter entirely.
